methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Cache Energy, a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Arpit Dwivedi, has raised $8.5M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector contains one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within narrow valuation tiers to support a robust peer-median approach; only the stage-progression method yielded reliable quantitative input.

Stage-progression analysis, applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $8.5M raised proxy, implies a valuation of $21M. This represents the primary triangulation anchor given data constraints. The single-method triangulation yields a range of $18M (low) to $24M (high), with $21M as the median point.

The analysis is constrained by sparse same-stage comparables in Climate & Energy and the absence of narrowly filtered peer valuations. The $18M–$24M range reflects reasonable bounds around the stage-progression output, but carries elevated uncertainty regarding whether this multiplier appropriately captures Cache Energy's specific risk and market position relative to the broader cohort. Additional validation through future funding rounds or tighter peer clustering would strengthen conviction in this range.
